speaker: gauge
text: This honeycomb is all hexagons. Bees should build circles. I'll show them.

speaker: fitz
text: Hexagons beat squares. A mathematician proved it. For equal cells on a flat surface, hexagons use the least wall. Less wall means less wax.

speaker: gauge
text: How do bees pull that off?

speaker: fitz
text: Nobody's sure. New cells start out round. Some scientists think warm wax pulls them into hexagons. Others filmed bees shaping the walls themselves.

speaker: gauge
text: Ooh, what else is built weird? Subscribe and let's find out.
